question: Which WCAG 2.2 thresholds should a live UI audit's in-page capture use for target size and text contrast, and how is large text defined in CSS pixels?
method: Read the dated WCAG 2.2 W3C Recommendation and the Understanding document for Success Criterion 1.4.3 over HTTPS and recorded the SHA-1 of each retrieved page. No other sources, tools, or provider calls were used. Only thresholds and definitions are recorded; no normative text was copied beyond short numeric facts.
queries: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) thresholds and large-scale text definition
WCAG 2.2 Success Criteria 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) and 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced)
Point to CSS pixel conversion for large-scale text
findings: SC 1.4.3 (Level AA) requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 for text, and at least 3 to 1 for large-scale text.
Large-scale text is at least 18 point, or 14 point bold; at 1pt = 1.333 CSS px that is about 24 CSS px, or about 18.7 CSS px when bold.
SC 2.5.8 (Level AA) requires pointer targets of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, with spacing, equivalent, inline, user agent control, and essential exceptions.
SC 2.5.5 (Level AAA) requires pointer targets of at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels, with equivalent, inline, user agent control, and essential exceptions.
adopted: Flag targets under 24 by 24 CSS pixels and treat 44 by 44 as an optional stricter bar.
Flag text contrast below 4.5 to 1, or below 3 to 1 for large text, and define large text in CSS pixels in the capture table.
List inline targets as a known false positive, matching the inline exception.
rejected: Treating the capture output as a conformance verdict; it is a screening signal that findings confirm against source and observation.
skipped: Non-text contrast, focus appearance, and the full conformance model, which the audit lenses cover qualitatively.
Automating the spacing exception of SC 2.5.8 in the capture script.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, W3C Recommendation 12 December 2024
findings: SC 1.4.3 sets 4.5 to 1 for text and 3 to 1 for large-scale text at Level AA.
SC 2.5.8 sets 24 by 24 CSS pixels at Level AA; SC 2.5.5 sets 44 by 44 CSS pixels at Level AAA.
Large scale means at least 18 point, or 14 point bold.

sources.title: Understanding Success Criterion 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum), WCAG 2.2
findings: Point sizes follow the CSS pt unit, with 1pt = 1.333px, so 18pt is about 24 CSS px and 14pt is about 18.5 to 18.7 CSS px.
